source_evidence.anchor: Introduction, paragraph defining SR_{p,r} and unit roundoff
source_evidence.observation: The paper uses p-1 fraction bits, r limited random bits, and unit roundoff u_p := 2^(1-p).
The arithmetic is a normalized precision-p binary floating-point system. An elementary operation rounded stochastically has multiplicative error bounded by u_p.
SR_{p,r}(x) rounds to one of the two enclosing precision-p values, with probability determined by fl_{p+r}(x). The p+r-bit directed-rounding error beta satisfies |beta| <= u_{p+r} = 2^(1-p-r).
For SR_{p,r}(x) = x(1+delta), E(delta) = beta = (fl_{p+r}(x)-x)/x, so limited-precision stochastic rounding is generally biased.
For successive operations, E(delta_k | delta_1,...,delta_{k-1}) = beta_k. When the exact pre-rounding result is zero, the proof sets delta_k = beta_k = 0.
If the conditional-bias relations hold and |beta_k| <= B, then (1-B)^m <= E[product_{k=1}^m(1+delta_k)] <= (1+B)^m.
For a in R^n, the paper defines y = sum_i a_i, kappa(a) = sum_i |a_i|/|sum_i a_i|, gamma_m(u) = (1+u)^m-1, the left-to-right SR_{p,r} recurrence, and its coefficientwise product representation.
The stated summation-bias bound is |E(hat_y)-y|/|y| <= kappa(a) gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r}).

Linearity, the triangle inequality, and Theorem 3.6 give a coefficientwise factor (1+u_{p+r})^(n-max{i,2}+1)-1, which is bounded by gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r}); summing |a_i| and dividing by |y| produces kappa(a).

binders: Fix the vector length n and an input vector a = (a_1,...,a_n) in R^n; n is implicitly a positive integer because it is a vector dimension and the recursion starts at index 1. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, Section 4.1 and equation (4.1).)

Fix precision p and a positive integer r specifying the limited number of random bits; u_p = 2^(1-p) and u_{p+r} = 2^(1-p-r). (PDF p. 3, printed B1229, introduction; PDF p. 6, printed B1232, Definition 2.9.)

For the fixed input, construct the random computed result hat_y using the successive SR_{p,r} rounding decisions, and take expectation over those decisions. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, recurrence and Theorem 4.1.)
hypotheses: The exact target is y = sum_{i=1}^n a_i. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.1).)

The computed recursion is hat_s_1 = a_1 and hat_s_k = SR_{p,r}(hat_s_{k-1}+a_k) = (hat_s_{k-1}+a_k)(1+delta_{k-1}) for k=2,...,n, with hat_y = hat_s_n. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, recursive-summation table.)
The corresponding exact recursion is s_1=a_1 and s_k=s_{k-1}+a_k, with y=s_n. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, recursive-summation table.)
Each stochastic rounding error satisfies |delta_{k-1}| <= u_p. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, paragraph following equation (4.4).)

For each addition, beta_{k-1} is the p+r-bit truncation error of hat_s_{k-1}+a_k, is bounded pathwise by u_{p+r}, and satisfies the inherited conditional relation E(delta_{k-1} | preceding rounding errors) = beta_{k-1}. (PDF p. 6, printed B1232, paragraph before Definition 2.9; PDF p. 8, printed B1234, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.5).)

To interpret the displayed relative bound and kappa(a) as real-valued quantities, y must be nonzero, although Theorem 4.1 does not state this hypothesis explicitly. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2) and (4.6).)
conclusions: The summation bias satisfies |E(hat_y)-y|/|y| <= kappa(a) gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r}). (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, Theorem 4.1, equation (4.6).)

Equivalently, after expanding the definitions, |E(hat_y)-y| <= (sum_{i=1}^n |a_i|) ((1+u_{p+r})^(n-1)-1). (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2), (4.3), and (4.6); PDF p. 14, printed B1240, final proof lines.)
For coefficient a_i, the proof uses |E[product_{k=max{i,2}}^n(1+delta_{k-1})]-1| <= (1+u_{p+r})^(n-max{i,2}+1)-1 <= gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r}). (PDF p. 14, printed B1240, proof of Theorem 4.1.)
definitions_and_conventions: kappa(a) := (sum_{i=1}^n |a_i|)/|sum_{i=1}^n a_i|. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.2).)
gamma_m(u) := (1+u)^m-1; equation (4.3) also gives gamma_m(u)=m u+O(u^2) when m u is much smaller than 1. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.3).)
The computed result has the exact product representation hat_y = sum_{i=1}^n a_i product_{k=max{i,2}}^n(1+delta_{k-1}). (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.4).)

beta_{k-1} := (fl_{p+r}(hat_s_{k-1}+a_k)-(hat_s_{k-1}+a_k))/(hat_s_{k-1}+a_k), subject to the zero-result convention inherited from Lemma 3.2. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.5); PDF p. 8, printed B1234, Lemma 3.2.)
An empty product is implicitly 1 where an index range is empty, notably for the n=1 edge case, although this convention is not restated in Section 4.1. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.4).)
implicit_context: The conditional-bias property and pathwise beta bound required by Theorem 3.6 are inherited from the general SR_{p,r} model; no independence or mean-independence assumption on the original delta errors is made. (PDF p. 8, printed B1234, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 9, printed B1235, Theorem 3.6.)
The expectation is taken after fixing a, n, p, and r; y is deterministic while hat_y is random. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.1), (4.4), and (4.6).)

The normalized floating-point model and relative-error formulas implicitly require operations to remain in the range where the enclosing floating-point values and multiplicative error model are defined. The paper does not state a separate no-overflow or no-underflow hypothesis here. (PDF p. 5, printed B1231, Section 2.2; PDF p. 13, printed B1239, recursive-summation setup.)
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result applies specifically to left-to-right recursive summation with n-1 additions, exact initialization hat_s_1=a_1, and one limited-precision stochastic rounding SR_{p,r} after each subsequent addition. It is not a pairwise, compensated, or high-probability summation result. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, Section 4.1 recurrence and Theorem 4.1.)
numerical_model: The base system is normalized binary precision-p floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff u_p=2^(1-p). (PDF p. 3, printed B1229, introduction; PDF p. 5, printed B1231, Section 2.2.)
SR_{p,r}(x) returns a precision-p enclosing value, but its Bernoulli probability is computed from the p+r-bit quantity fl_{p+r}(x). (PDF p. 6, printed B1232, Definition 2.9 and equation (2.6).)
Limited-precision SR is biased: E[SR_{p,r}(x)] = fl_{p+r}(x), and if SR_{p,r}(x)=x(1+delta), then E(delta)=beta. (PDF p. 7, printed B1233, equation (3.1).)

The stochastic rounding error is bounded by u_p, while the directed p+r-bit truncation error governing the bias is bounded by u_{p+r}. (PDF p. 6, printed B1232, paragraph before Definition 2.9; PDF p. 13, printed B1239, paragraph following equation (4.4).)
error_notions: The bounded quantity is relative absolute bias, |E(hat_y)-y|/|y|. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.6).)

It is not E(|hat_y-y|)/|y|, not a bound on each realization, and not a high-probability forward-error bound. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 14, printed B1240, transition to the distinct probabilistic Theorem 4.2.)

The local delta variables are relative stochastic rounding errors, while beta variables are relative p+r-bit directed-rounding errors controlling their conditional means. (PDF p. 7, printed B1233, equation (3.1); PDF p. 8, printed B1234, Lemma 3.2.)
norms: All displayed error magnitudes use the scalar absolute value. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2) and (4.6).)
The numerator sum_i |a_i| in kappa(a) is the vector l1 norm written componentwise; no other vector norm occurs in Theorem 4.1. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.2).)
constants_and_indexing: There are n-1 rounding errors, indexed delta_1,...,delta_{n-1}; addition k uses delta_{k-1}. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, recursive-summation table.)
Coefficient a_i is multiplied by errors with k=max{i,2},...,n, so it contains L_i=n-max{i,2}+1 factors. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.4); PDF p. 14, printed B1240, proof.)
The common worst-case factor count is n-1, producing gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r})=(1+u_{p+r})^(n-1)-1. (PDF p. 14, printed B1240, proof of Theorem 4.1.)
u_{p+r}=2^(1-p-r), not u_p+r and not u_p+u_r. (PDF p. 3, printed B1229, definition of u_p; PDF p. 6, printed B1232, bound |beta|<=2^(1-p-r)=u_{p+r}.)
higher_order_terms: The theorem uses the exact function gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r})=(1+u_{p+r})^(n-1)-1, so no higher-order term is omitted from the bound. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.3) and (4.6).)

The expression gamma_m(u)=m u+O(u^2) for m u much smaller than 1 is only an accompanying small-u expansion, not an additional hypothesis needed for the exact inequality. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.3).)
exceptional_values: If an exact pre-rounding operation result is zero, Lemma 3.2 sets its delta and beta errors to zero, resolving the relative-error formula's zero denominator. (PDF p. 8, printed B1234, proof of Lemma 3.2.)
If the final exact sum y is zero, both kappa(a) and the relative bias in (4.6) divide by zero; the paper gives no convention for this case. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2) and (4.6).)

The paper's normalized finite-exponent model does not state how Theorem 4.1 handles overflow, underflow, subnormal values, infinities, or NaNs. (PDF p. 5, printed B1231, Section 2.2; PDF p. 13, printed B1239, theorem setup.)

undebatable_constraints: The conclusion must retain the factor kappa(a); replacing it by 1 would require an unstated sign or conditioning assumption on the summands. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2) and (4.6).)
The gamma index is n-1, corresponding to the n-1 rounded additions. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.6); PDF p. 14, printed B1240, proof.)
The precision entering the bias factor is u_{p+r}, whereas u_p bounds individual stochastic rounding errors. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, paragraph after equation (4.4) and equation (4.6).)
The result concerns |E(hat_y)-y|, not E|hat_y-y| and not a realization-wise error. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.6).)

No independence assumption may be added; the derivation uses conditional expected errors beta_k and their uniform bound through Theorem 3.6. (PDF p. 8, printed B1234, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 9, printed B1235, Theorem 3.6.)
The algorithm is the stated left-to-right recursive sum with exact initialization and n-1 SR_{p,r}-rounded additions. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, recursive-summation table.)
The exact gamma function retains all powers of u_{p+r}; the small-u big-O expansion is not the theorem's conclusion. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.3) and (4.6).)
A real-valued reading of the relative statement requires y=sum_i a_i to be nonzero because both sides contain |y| in a denominator. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2) and (4.6).)

ambiguities.issue: The theorem does not explicitly assume y != 0.
ambiguities.evidence: Both kappa(a) in (4.2) and the left side of (4.6) divide by |y|, with no zero-sum convention stated. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.2) and (4.6).)
ambiguities.impact: The ordinary real-valued contract must either add y != 0 as an implicit well-definedness condition or leave the zero-sum case outside the theorem's domain.

ambiguities.issue: Input representability and exceptional floating-point range behavior are not specified in Section 4.1.
ambiguities.evidence: The section binds a in R^n and sets hat_s_1=a_1, while the earlier model describes a normalized finite-exponent floating-point system; no no-overflow, no-underflow, or a_i in F assumption is stated. (PDF p. 5, printed B1231, Section 2.2; PDF p. 13, printed B1239, Section 4.1 recurrence.)
ambiguities.impact: One must not silently strengthen the theorem to representable inputs or silently assign IEEE exceptional-value semantics; only the abstract relative-error model is supported.

ambiguities.issue: Equation (4.5) is syntactically undefined when hat_s_{k-1}+a_k=0.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.5) divides by the pre-rounding sum, while the proof of Lemma 3.2 separately declares delta_k=beta_k=0 when the corresponding exact operation result is zero. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equation (4.5); PDF p. 8, printed B1234, Lemma 3.2 proof.)
ambiguities.impact: A complete formalization must import the zero-result convention rather than treating (4.5) as an unrestricted quotient.

ambiguities.issue: The prose after (4.6) refers to gamma_n(u_{p+r}), although the displayed theorem and proof use gamma_{n-1}(u_{p+r}).
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.6) displays gamma_{n-1}, its following sentence names gamma_n as the function defined in (4.3), and the proof ends with gamma_{n-1}. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 14, printed B1240, proof.)
ambiguities.impact: The displayed equation and proof agree on n-1, so the contract uses n-1 and treats the prose as a generic reference to the gamma family rather than a competing bound.

ambiguities.issue: The exact directed mode used for fl_{p+r} is not uniquely fixed by the general definition.
ambiguities.evidence: The setup describes truncation to p+r bits but immediately notes that fl_{p+r} could use another directed rounding mode, all satisfying |beta|<=u_{p+r}. (PDF p. 6, printed B1232, paragraph before Definition 2.9.)
ambiguities.impact: Theorem 4.1 depends on the directed-error bound and conditional-bias model, not on a uniquely selected directed mode beyond those properties.

contract_plain_english: Fix a real vector a and compute its sum by the stated left-to-right recursion, applying limited-precision stochastic rounding SR_{p,r} after each of the n-1 additions. The expected computed sum may be biased because its rounding probabilities use only p+r bits, but the absolute relative bias is at most the summation condition number kappa(a) times (1+u_{p+r})^(n-1)-1. This is an expectation-level bias bound, not a bound on individual runs or an expected absolute error, and it is ordinarily meaningful only when the exact sum is nonzero. (PDF p. 13, printed B1239, equations (4.1)-(4.6); PDF p. 14, printed B1240, proof of Theorem 4.1.)
